ev.f_m_easter.text.1: Easter night: the church is a sea of candle flames, and when the singing breaks out — Christ is risen! — you feel the whole year was waiting for this moment.
ev.f_m_easter.text.2: After the long fast, the Easter table. The first bite of meat and cheese tastes better than any banquet, and neighbours embrace right in the street.
ev.f_m_easter.text.3: At Easter you carried a candle flame from the church all the way home, shielding it from the wind with your palm. It made it — and you walked tall all evening.
ev.f_m_easter.text.2.tewahedo: Fifty-five days of fasting are over. The Easter service went on until cockcrow, and then the whole neighbourhood broke the fast together — injera, meat and laughter till morning.
ev.f_m_easter.text.3.orthodox: At Easter you were given an egg dyed red as the feast itself. You knocked eggs with the neighbours' children and won three times running.
ev.f_m_christmas.text.1: Christmas night. The service was long and you kept nodding off, until the singing woke you — you still remember how it rang under the vaults.
ev.f_m_christmas.text.2: At Christmas every house smelled of baking and woodsmoke, beggars were called to the table, and quarrels were put off for better days.
ev.f_m_christmas.text.2.tewahedo: At Genna, the Ethiopian Christmas, young men chased a wooden ball with curved sticks until dark, and at night everyone stood in white at the candlelit service.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.1: On the feast of the local patron saint, banners were carried through the streets and a fair buzzed on the square until evening. You spent every coin you had on sweets.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.2: On his feast day it is as if the saint himself walks among the people: doors stand open, the church is packed, and old folk recall his miracles as if they had seen them yesterday.
ev.f_m_lent.text.1: Lent: no meat, no milk, no butter. By the third week you dreamed of cheese; by the fifth you stopped thinking about it and felt a strange lightness.
ev.f_m_lent.text.2: In Lent the whole town grows quieter: less noise in the taverns, more people in church at dusk. Even the market traders lower their voices.
ev.f_m_lent.text.1.tewahedo: Fasting in Ethiopia is strict: not a crumb until the middle of the day, then only beans, lentils and injera. You got used to it, and there was a quiet pride in that.
ev.f_m_icon_procession.text: A wonder-working icon was carried through the town. People knelt right in the dust; you squeezed to the front and for a moment met its gaze — a dark face with enormous eyes.
ev.f_m_icon_lamp.text: An icon lamp glowed all night in the corner before the icons. You fell asleep watching its tiny flame, and nothing felt frightening.
ev.f_m_bells.text: You tried to count the strokes of the bell, but on the feast day every bell tower rang at once, and the count drowned in a roar that made the ground tremble.
ev.f_m_bells.text.BYZ: A monk walked around the church striking a long wooden board — the semantron — with a mallet. The rhythm carried across the whole district, and you learned to tap it out on your palms.
ev.f_m_timkat.text.1: Timkat: priests in embroidered robes carried the tabot, wrapped in brocade, down to the water under umbrellas of every colour. At dawn the water was blessed, and the crowd rushed laughing into the spray.
ev.f_m_timkat.text.2: All night before Timkat fires burned by the water and people sang. You fell asleep on your cloak and woke to drums and the jingle of sistra.
ev.f_m_meskel.text: For Meskel a huge bonfire, the demera, was built and crowned with a cross and yellow flowers. When it collapsed, the old men argued for ages over which way the top had fallen and what it foretold.
ev.f_m_ramadan.text.1: Ramadan. Not a sip of water all day; at sunset the whole town holds its breath for the call to prayer. A date and a mouthful of water are never so good as in that minute.
ev.f_m_ramadan.text.2: At night in Ramadan the streets come alive: lanterns, sweet stalls, guests going from house to house. Before dawn a drummer walked the quarter, waking everyone for the last meal.
ev.f_m_ramadan.text.3: In the last nights of Ramadan you prayed late: they say one of them is the Night of Power, better than a thousand months. No one knows which, so no one sleeps.
ev.f_m_eid_fitr.text.1: Eid al-Fitr! New clothes, sweets, and everyone you meet wishes you a blessed feast. You made the rounds of half the quarter and came home with your pockets full.
ev.f_m_eid_fitr.text.2: On the morning of the feast, before the prayer, every household gave its measure of grain to the poor. Even the poorest yard has bread today.
ev.f_m_eid_adha.text: For Eid al-Adha rams were slaughtered in the yards. The meat was split three ways — for the household, for friends, for the poor — and by evening the whole quarter smelled of smoke and spices.
ev.f_m_friday.text.1: Friday prayer in the great mosque: thousands rise and bow at once, like a field under the wind. You left your shoes among hundreds by the door and spent half an hour finding yours afterwards.
ev.f_m_friday.text.2: The Friday sermon was about honest scales in the market. Two shopkeepers beside you visibly squirmed.
ev.f_m_quran_school.text: At the Quran school you recited the first sura by heart without a single stumble. The teacher nodded, and a honey cake was waiting for you at home.
ev.f_m_passover.text.1: The Passover seder: bitter herbs, unleavened bread, wine. The youngest at the table asked the questions, and the elders answered with the story of the Exodus — as if they had been there themselves.
ev.f_m_passover.text.2: Before Passover the house was scoured for every last crumb of leaven. You crawled under the benches with a candle and found a forgotten crust — to general horror and laughter.
ev.f_m_sabbath.text.1: On Friday before sunset the Sabbath candles were lit. Work stopped; the town beyond the wall went on bustling, but the house grew quiet, as if time itself had decided to rest.
ev.f_m_sabbath.text.2: The Sabbath: no fire, no work, only prayer, a slow meal and talk. You learned to treasure the one day when no one hurries anywhere.
ev.f_m_yom_kippur.text: Yom Kippur: a day without food or water, everyone in white, asking forgiveness of God and of one another in the synagogue. When the shofar sounded, you felt light, as if after a long illness.
ev.f_m_sukkot.text: For Sukkot a booth of branches was built in the yard. You begged to sleep in it and spent the night watching the stars through the leaves.
ev.f_m_diwali.text.1: Diwali: a clay lamp on every ledge, threshold and step. You helped pour the oil, and by nightfall the whole street glowed as if the stars had come down to visit.
ev.f_m_diwali.text.2: On Diwali night the doors are left open so that the goddess Lakshmi can find her way in. You guarded the threshold till midnight, just in case.
ev.f_m_holi.text: Holi! It's spring, and everyone pelts everyone with coloured powder and water. You came home pink, yellow and green all over, and nobody could tell where your clothes ended.
ev.f_m_chariot.text: For the temple festival the god rode out on a colossal chariot taller than the houses. Thousands hauled on the ropes; you grabbed one too, if only for a minute — they say it washes away sins.
ev.f_m_holy_river.text.1: At dawn you stepped into the sacred river along with hundreds of others. The water is cold, the sun is rising, and everyone scoops it up in their palms and pours it back as an offering.
ev.f_m_holy_river.text.2: In the evening lamps in leaf-boats were set afloat on the river. Your little flame drifted a long way without going out — a good sign, said the old woman beside you.
ev.f_m_vesak.text.1: On the Buddha's birthday a small statue was bathed in fragrant water. You queued up and poured a ladleful over it, gently, as if over a real baby.
ev.f_m_vesak.text.2: On the Buddha's feast hundreds of lamps were lit in the monastery courtyard, and the monks chanted sutras late into the night. You didn't follow the words, but the rhythm rocked you like the surf.
ev.f_m_alms.text: In the morning a monk with a bowl stopped at the door — silent, eyes lowered. You put a handful of food in his bowl, and somehow the whole day felt brighter.
ev.f_m_temple_bell.text: The monastery's evening bell carries across the whole valley. You stopped what you were doing and listened until the hum melted away completely.
ev.f_m_ghost_festival.text.1: During the festival for the souls of the dead, lanterns were set floating down the river for those who have gone. The lights drifted into the dark, and it felt as if someone on the far bank were waiting for them.
ev.f_m_ghost_festival.text.2: For the festival of spirits, food was set out at the gates for hungry ghosts. You wanted to pinch a dumpling but thought better of it in time: who knows whose it is now.
ev.f_m_paryushana.text: Paryushana — eight days of fasting and repentance. On the last day you asked forgiveness of everyone you might have hurt that year, and heard the same words in reply: 'Micchami dukkadam.'
ev.f_m_ahimsa.text: You watched an old monk brush ants from the path with a soft whisk before each step. Ever since, you've watched where you put your own feet.
ev.f_m_cn_new_year.text.1: New Year: fresh door gods on the gate, red strips with good wishes, bamboo crackling in the fire to scare off evil spirits. You stayed up till dawn, as one must, so that the year will be long.
ev.f_m_cn_new_year.text.2: On the first day of the year the young bowed to their elders, and the elders handed children coins strung on red thread. You counted yours three times.
ev.f_m_qingming.text: Qingming: everyone went to the ancestors' graves — to pull the weeds, tidy the mound, set out food and burn paper money. On the way back the boys flew kites.
ev.f_m_kitchen_god.text: Before New Year the Kitchen God goes up to heaven to report on the household. His lips were smeared with sticky malt sugar so he'd say only sweet things. You thought this was cheating but kept quiet.
ev.f_m_lantern.text: The Lantern Festival: the whole town out in the streets, lanterns shaped like fish, hares and lotuses, riddles pinned to them. You solved one and won a cake as a prize.
ev.f_m_matsuri.text.1: Matsuri! Young men carried the portable shrine through the streets, swinging it so hard the kami must have felt seasick. Drums, shouts, flutes — you were hoarse by evening.
ev.f_m_matsuri.text.2: At the shrine festival grilled rice cakes and toys were sold by the gate, and on the stage dancers performed sacred kagura. You watched open-mouthed.
ev.f_m_shrine_new_year.text: In the first days of the year you went to the local shrine: tug the bell rope, clap twice, ask the kami for a good year. The frost nipped your ears.
ev.f_m_purification.text: For the midsummer purification you cut a little paper figure, breathed your troubles onto it and set it floating down the river. You felt lighter — or imagined you did.
ev.f_m_saturnalia.text.1: Saturnalia! For a week nobody works, everyone exchanges candles and clay figurines, and servants sit at table beside their masters. You won a whole handful of nuts at games.
ev.f_m_saturnalia.text.2: At the Parilia people leapt over bonfires, livestock and all, and sang through the night. You jumped three times without singeing a hair.
ev.f_m_saturnalia.text.1.athens: The Panathenaea: a new peplos for Athena was carried through the city — a huge embroidered cloth like a sail. You ran after the procession all the way to the Acropolis.
ev.f_m_saturnalia.text.2.athens: At the Great Dionysia you spent the whole day in the theatre: three tragedies and a comedy. The whole city laughed at the comedy and wept at the tragedies.
ev.f_m_lares.text: Every morning a cake and a pinch of salt are left at the household shrine for the lares, the spirits of the home. Today, for the first time, you were trusted to do it yourself.
ev.f_m_lares.text.athens: Before a meal the first morsel goes into the hearth for Hestia, keeper of the home. Today, for the first time, that task was yours.
ev.f_m_opet.text.1: The Opet Festival: the god's barque was carried out of the temple on the priests' shoulders. People crowded the road and put questions to the god, and the barque swayed in answer — yes or no.
ev.f_m_opet.text.2: The Beautiful Feast of the Valley: people crossed the river to their ancestors' tombs with flowers, beer and food, and feasted right by the entrances until night. The dead need cheer too.
ev.f_m_nile_rise.text: The Nile has begun to rise — a new year! Everyone poured onto the bank: rising water means bread. The priests marked the level on the steps, and you cheered every handspan.
ev.f_m_akitu.text: Akitu, the New Year festival: Marduk's statue was paraded along the Processional Way, followed by other gods who had arrived by boat. They say the priest even slapped the king — if he wept, the year would be good.
ev.f_m_ishtar_feast.text: On the night of the new moon fires were lit by the temple and hymns sung to Sin, the Moon god. You made a wish looking at the thin crescent and told no one.
ev.f_m_kupala.text: On Kupala night couples leapt over bonfires, girls floated wreaths down the river, and the boldest went into the forest to look for the fern flower. You came back without the flower, but happy.
ev.f_m_spring_feast.text: Seeing off the winter: round flatbreads like little suns, sledding down the hill, and a straw effigy of winter burned with songs beyond the village fence.
ev.f_m_wayeb.text: Five nameless days at the year's end — Wayeb. No one washes their hair, starts anything new or leaves the house without need: in these days the wall between worlds is thin.
ev.f_m_new_fire.text: A bundle of years has ended: every fire in the valley was put out and the old pots smashed. All night people waited to see whether the sun would be reborn. When the New Fire blazed on the mountain, you wept with everyone.
ev.f_m_rain_feast.text: The rain god's festival: dancers in feathers whirled on the plaza to conch trumpets and drums, and priests sent copal smoke up to the sky. By evening clouds really did gather.
ev.f_m_rain_feast.text.maya_gods: The festival of Chaak, the rain god: dancers in feathers whirled on the plaza to conch trumpets and drums, and priests sent copal smoke up to the sky. By evening clouds really did gather.
ev.f_m_rain_feast.text.aztec_gods: The festival of Tlaloc, the rain god: dancers in feathers whirled on the plaza to conch trumpets and drums, and priests sent copal smoke up to the sky. By evening clouds really did gather.
ev.f_m_inti_raymi.text: Inti Raymi, the festival of the Sun on the shortest day of the year: at dawn everyone turned east to await Inti's return. Then came chicha, dancing and feasting till dark.
ev.f_m_pachamama.text.1: Before drinking your chicha you splashed a few drops onto the ground for Pachamama. Everyone does, and they say the earth remembers.
ev.f_m_pachamama.text.2: Before sowing, an offering was buried in the field: coca leaves, maize, a scrap of fat. Pachamama is hungry after the winter.
ev.f_m_masks.text: The masks came out of the forest — tall, draped in raffia and feathers, with carved faces. The grown-ups said these were spirits come to visit. You hid behind the crowd but couldn't take your eyes off them.
ev.f_m_ancestors_feast.text.1: At the harvest feast the first handful of new millet went to the ancestors, and the elder poured beer on the ground, naming them one by one, for a long, long time.
ev.f_m_ancestors_feast.text.2: At night by the fire an old storyteller sang of heroes of long ago, and you understood that here the past has not passed: it sits beside you at the fire.
ev.f_m_nowruz.text: Nowruz, the new year on the spring equinox: sprouted greens on the table, new clothes, sweets and guests. Everyone wishes everyone a good year, thirteen days in a row.
ev.f_m_fire_temple.text: In the fire temple burns a flame they say has not gone out for hundreds of years. The priest, his mouth veiled so his breath would not defile it, added sandalwood, and the scent filled the hall.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.title: Pilgrimage
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.text: Pilgrims bound for the Holy Land pass through town — to Jerusalem, to the Holy Sepulchre. They invite you along: the road is long and dangerous, but those who reach it are said to come back cleansed.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.go.success: The road was long, but you made it. Standing before the shrine, you understood what it had all been for. You came home a different person, and everyone noticed.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.go_poor: Go as a poor pilgrim, living on alms and prayer
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.go_poor.succes: People along the way fed you, gave you a roof and shared their water. You got there and back — with empty hands and a full heart.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.go_poor.failur: The road was harder than you thought: cold, hunger, ruined feet. You came back ill, but you regret nothing.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.offering: Stay, and send a gift and a prayer with the pilgrims
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.stay: Not now: home and work won't let you go
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.text.catholic: Pilgrims with scallop shells on their hats pass through town, bound for Santiago de Compostela and the tomb of Saint James; others are heading to Rome and the tombs of the apostles Peter and Paul. They invite you along: a long road, but grace is worth it.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.text.tewahedo: Pilgrims are heading to Aksum, to the church of St Mary of Zion, where the Ark of the Covenant itself is said to rest. They invite you along: weeks of travel over mountains and gorges.
ev.f_pilgrimage_christian.text.RUS: Wanderers are heading to Kiev, to the Caves Monastery, to venerate the saints who rest in the caves; the boldest go further still, to the Holy Sepulchre. They invite you along: a long way through forests and over rivers, with bandits on the roads.
ev.f_pilgrimage_hajj.title: The hajj
ev.f_pilgrimage_hajj.text: A caravan is forming for Mecca. The hajj is a duty for everyone who is able, once in a lifetime. The road is long and dangerous, but those who return are greeted with honour and called hajji.
ev.f_pilgrimage_hajj.go.success: You circled the Kaaba in white ihram among people from every corner of the earth — dark and fair, rich and poor — and all were equal. Now the honoured title 'hajji' is added to your name.
ev.f_pilgrimage_hajj.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.

ev.f_pilgrimage_jerusalem.title: To Jerusalem
ev.f_pilgrimage_jerusalem.text: A few members of the community are setting out for Jerusalem, to see the holy city with their own eyes and pray there. The way is long and unsafe, but it is the dream of a lifetime.
ev.f_pilgrimage_jerusalem.go.success: You stood on the stones of Jerusalem and could not hold back your tears. You brought a handful of its earth home in a knotted cloth.
ev.f_pilgrimage_jerusalem.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.

ev.f_pilgrimage_kashi.title: Pilgrimage to Kashi
ev.f_pilgrimage_kashi.text: Pilgrims are going to Kashi, the holy city on the Ganges: to bathe in its waters is to wash away the sins of many lives. The way is long, through forests and foreign kingdoms, but they invite you along.
ev.f_pilgrimage_kashi.go.success: At dawn you went down the steps of the ghat into the Ganges. All around people sang and bells rang, and you felt your life beginning again.
ev.f_pilgrimage_kashi.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.

ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.title: Pilgrimage
ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.text: Monks and laypeople are setting out for a famous monastery on a sacred mountain. They say whoever reaches it and bows there gains merit for many rebirths to come.
ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.go.success: You climbed thousands of steps to the monastery, and when the bell struck it seemed the sound came from inside you.
ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.

ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.text.CHN: Monks and laypeople are setting out for Mount Wutai, where the bodhisattva Manjushri is said to appear. Whoever reaches it and bows there gains merit for many rebirths to come.
ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.text.JPN: Pilgrims are setting out for Mount Koya, to the monastery of the great teacher Kukai, or on the circuit of the temples of merciful Kannon. Whoever completes the way gains merit for many rebirths to come.
ev.f_pilgrimage_buddhist.text.IND: Pilgrims are going to Bodh Gaya, to the tree beneath which the Buddha attained awakening. Whoever bows there gains merit for many rebirths to come.
ev.f_pilgrimage_ise.title: Pilgrimage to Ise
ev.f_pilgrimage_ise.text: The neighbours are gathering a party for a pilgrimage to Ise, to the great shrine of the Sun goddess Amaterasu. The road is long and the inns are not cheap, but those who have been talk about it into old age.
ev.f_pilgrimage_ise.go.success: You passed under the great torii, washed your hands in the Isuzu River and bowed to the goddess. You brought home amulets, and now the neighbours come to you for them.
ev.f_pilgrimage_ise.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.
ev.f_pilgrimage_ise.go_poor: Go as a poor pilgrim, living on alms and prayer

ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.title: To the sanctuary
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text: People are setting out for a great sanctuary where, they say, the gods hear better than anywhere else. The way is long and the gifts must be rich, but a question asked there can change a life.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.go.success: You arrived, brought your gifts and received an answer. You still read its meaning in different ways, but peace came to your heart.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.

ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text.roman_god: Acquaintances are setting out for Delphi to ask Apollo, through the Pythia, about their fate. A journey by sea and over mountains, and the gifts must be generous, but who has not dreamed of hearing the god's own answer?
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text.athens: In autumn a sacred procession goes from Athens to Eleusis — initiation into the Mysteries of Demeter and Persephone. The initiated, they say, no longer fear death. But you must fast, pay the priests and keep silent about all you see.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text.egyptian_: Pilgrims are sailing to Abydos, to the tomb of Osiris, to leave a stela with a prayer and see the sacred mysteries. It is a long way down the Nile, but there, they say, the living and the dead are closest.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text.mesopotam: People are setting out for Babylon, to the temple of Esagila, to bow to Marduk and ask the priests about their fate. The road along the river is long, and nomads raid the steppe.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sanctuary.text.slavic_pa: People are setting out for the great sanctuary on the hill where Perun's idol stands. The way runs through forests and marshes, and the gifts must be generous, but there, they say, the gods hear every word.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.title: Pilgrimage
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.text: People are setting out for a great sanctuary far away, where pilgrims gather from every corner of the land. The way is long and the gifts must be rich, but the gods there are said to be especially merciful.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.go.success: You made it, brought your gifts and stood among thousands of people speaking different tongues but praying for the same things. You came home with a light heart.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.go_poor: Go as a poor pilgrim, living on alms and prayer
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.go_poor.success: People along the way fed you, gave you a roof and shared their water. You got there and back — with empty hands and a full heart.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.go_poor.failure: The road was harder than you thought: cold, hunger, ruined feet. You came back ill, but you regret nothing.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.offering: Stay, and send a gift and a prayer with the pilgrims
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.stay: Not now: home and work won't let you go
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.text.maya_gods: People are setting out for the island of Cozumel, to the shrine of Ix Chel, goddess of the moon and of birth, or to the Sacred Cenote, the rain god's well. The way runs through the forest and over the sea, and the gifts must be rich.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.text.aztec_gods: Pilgrims are going to Cholula, to the great pyramid of Quetzalcoatl. People come there from every corner of the land, and the gods there are said to be especially merciful.
ev.f_pilgrimage_americas.text.andean: Pilgrims are going to Pachacamac, to the oracle revered even by the Inca, or to Lake Titicaca, where the Sun was born from the waters. The way over the mountain passes is long, and the gifts must be rich.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.title: Pilgrimage
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.text: People are setting out for a distant holy place of which wonders are told. The way is long and the gifts must be generous, but to go there even once is the dream of a lifetime.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.go.success: The road was long, but you made it. Standing before the shrine, you understood what it had all been for. You came home a different person, and everyone noticed.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.go.failure: A fever laid you low on the road, and on the way back you were robbed. You did reach the shrine, but came home gaunt and nearly penniless.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.go_poor: Go as a poor pilgrim, living on alms and prayer
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.go_poor.suc: People along the way fed you, gave you a roof and shared their water. You got there and back — with empty hands and a full heart.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.go_poor.fai: The road was harder than you thought: cold, hunger, ruined feet. You came back ill, but you regret nothing.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.offering: Stay, and send a gift and a prayer with the pilgrims
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.stay: Not now: home and work won't let you go
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.text.africa: People are setting out for a sacred grove far beyond the river, where a mighty spirit dwells, to ask for children, rain and luck. The way is long, and the grove has its own strict laws.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.text.zoroas: People are setting out for a great fire temple where the flame is said to have burned since the days of the ancient kings. The road over the mountains is long, and the gifts must be generous.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.text.chines: Pilgrims are going to Mount Tai to bow to the lord of the mountain, who rules over life and death. To climb to its summit even once is the dream of a lifetime.
ev.f_pilgrimage_sacred_place.text.jain: Pilgrims are going to the sacred mountain of Shatrunjaya, where hundreds of temples crown the summit like a white city. The climb must be made on foot, fasting and in prayer.
ev.f_monk.title: The monastery
ev.f_monk.text: The {g:abbot of the local monastery|abbess of the local convent} has had an eye on you for a while. 'You have a quiet heart,' {g:he|she} said. 'The world is noisy, and we have a place for you.'
ev.f_monk.text.chinese_folk: A Daoist master from a mountain retreat has had an eye on you for a while. 'You have a quiet heart,' he said. 'The world is noisy, and in the mountains there is room for one who seeks the Way.'
ev.f_monk.text.shinto: The head priest of the Buddhist temple beside the local shrine has had an eye on you for a while. 'You have a quiet heart,' he said. 'The world is noisy, and we have a place for you.'
ev.f_monk.vows: Take vows and enter the monastery
ev.f_monk.vows.ok: You took your vows. A new name, new clothes, a new life — and a surprising quiet inside.
ev.f_monk.later: Promise to think about it — someday
ev.f_monk.refuse: No: my place is in the world
ev.f_monk_late.title: Leaving the world
ev.f_monk_late.text: The years have passed and much lies behind you. More and more you think of spending your remaining days in a monastery, in silence and prayer, as many have done before you.
ev.f_monk_late.go: Give part of your property to the monastery and take vows
ev.f_monk_late.give: Make a generous gift but stay at home
ev.f_monk_late.stay: No, the bustle of the world still holds you
ev.f_vow.title: A vow
ev.f_vow.text: On that terrible night when the storm nearly tore the house down, you swore that if you survived you would bring a rich gift to the temple. The storm passed. It's time to pay.
ev.f_vow.text.islamic: On that terrible night when the storm nearly tore the house down, you swore to God that if you survived you would feed forty poor people. The storm passed. It's time to keep your vow.
ev.f_vow.text.jewish: On that terrible night when the storm nearly tore the house down, you swore that if you survived you would give generously to the synagogue and the poor. The storm passed. It's time to keep your vow.
ev.f_vow.pay_small: Give what you can — heaven will understand
ev.f_vow.forget: People promise anything when they're afraid… Forget it
ev.f_charity.title: Alms
ev.f_charity.text: The time has come to give your due to the poor and the temple. The neighbours know how much you have, and they are watching to see how much you give.
ev.f_charity.text.islamic: It is time to pay the zakat — a fortieth of your savings, for the poor and the needy. It is not a kindness but a duty: wealth is purified when it is shared.
ev.f_charity.text.christian: The church is collecting its tithe, and beggars sit at the church gates. A neighbour has already boasted of how much he gave.
ev.f_charity.text.jewish: The community's collector goes from house to house: for the poor, for widows, for ransoming captives. Everyone has their share.
ev.f_charity.text.dharmic: It is the season of offerings: generosity is the first of virtues, and every gift, they say, returns in this life or the next. The monks and the temple are waiting.
ev.f_charity.dodge.success: No one suspected a thing. Only your heart is uneasy.
ev.f_charity.dodge.failure: The neighbours saw right through it. Now the whole quarter gossips about your stinginess.
ev.f_fasting.title: Fasting and work
ev.f_fasting.text: The fast has fallen in the hardest season of work. By midday your hands are shaking, and half the day is still ahead. You could ease off a little — who would see?
ev.f_fasting.text.islamic: Ramadan has fallen in the hot months. Not a sip of water from dawn to dusk, and the work won't wait: by midday circles swim before your eyes.
ev.f_fasting.text.jain: You took a long fast upon yourself — only boiled water, and only until sunset. On the fifth day your body begs for mercy.
ev.f_fasting.strict: Keep the fast strictly, whatever it costs
ev.f_fasting.ease: Keep it, but without being too hard on yourself
ev.f_preacher.title: The preacher
ev.f_preacher.text: A foreign preacher is speaking in the square. His faith is {other_faith}, and he speaks of it so warmly and simply that a crowd has gathered. Some laugh; others listen, holding their breath.
ev.f_preacher.convert: Follow him and accept his faith
ev.f_preacher.convert.ok: You never expected such a step from yourself. The neighbours look at you askance, but there is a new, unfamiliar light inside.
ev.f_preacher.dispute.success: You spoke so convincingly that the crowd began to drift away. The preacher bowed to you as to a worthy opponent.
ev.f_preacher.dispute.failure: He answered every argument you made, and now the crowd was laughing at you.
ev.f_preacher.bread: Give him some bread: he has a long road ahead
ev.f_mixed_love.title: A different faith
ev.f_mixed_love.text: You have fallen in love with someone of another faith — {other_faith}. Stolen meetings, talks till dawn. But there is no wedding without the community's blessing: one of you will have to give way.
ev.f_mixed_love.convert: Take up your beloved's faith and marry
ev.f_mixed_love.both: Marry, and let each of you pray in your own way
ev.f_mixed_love.both.success: There was plenty of gossip, but you held firm. At home you keep two customs and one life.
ev.f_mixed_love.both.failure: Both communities closed ranks against you. There will be no wedding — you were torn apart.
ev.f_doubt.title: Doubt
ev.f_doubt.text: You prayed and brought offerings, and still misfortune came — not to the wicked, but to the best people you know. For the first time a thought rang out: is anyone listening?
ev.f_doubt.counsel: Seek counsel from the wisest servant of the faith
ev.f_doubt.silent: Keep the rites and say nothing
ev.f_doubt.reason: Look for answers in reason and books
ev.f_omen_sky.title: An omen
ev.f_omen_sky.text: In broad daylight the sun began to go dark, as if something were taking bites out of it. Dogs howled, birds fell silent, people dropped to their knees. A few minutes later the light returned — but what was it?
ev.f_omen_sky.sign: It's a sign: pray and repent
ev.f_omen_sky.explain: Tell the neighbours that learned men can predict such things in advance
ev.f_omen_sky.explain.success: They heard you out, and someone even recalled the stargazers saying something like it. You gained a name as someone who knows things.
ev.f_omen_sky.explain.failure: They looked at you as if you were godless. People still bring it up.
ev.f_omen_sky.hide: Lock yourself in at home and wait it out
ev.f_miracle.title: A miracle
ev.f_miracle.text: A neighbour who had not left her bed for years suddenly walked again after someone brought her water from a holy spring. The whole quarter is buzzing, and people are already streaming to the spring.
ev.f_miracle.tell: Spread the news all over town
ev.f_relic.title: A relic for sale
ev.f_relic.text: A travelling merchant shows you a little casket: inside, he swears, is a fragment of a holy martyr's relics, with seal and certificate. He asks a high price, but promises the relic will protect the house from sickness and fire.
ev.f_relic.text.buddhist: A travelling merchant shows you a little casket: inside, he swears, is a sarira — a pearl-like relic left after a holy monk's cremation. He asks a high price, but promises the relic will bring blessings to the house.
ev.f_relic.buy.success: Knowledgeable people examined the relic and declared it genuine. Now people come to venerate it at your home.
ev.f_relic.buy.failure: A month later the same merchant was caught in the next town with a dozen identical caskets. People are laughing at you.
ev.f_relic.haggle.success: The merchant halved his price — suspiciously easily. Still, the relic sits on the shelf and your heart is at peace.
ev.f_relic.haggle.failure: The merchant took offence and went off to your neighbour.
ev.f_relic.expose.success: He got tangled in his own stories and fled. The whole quarter is talking about how you exposed the fraud.
ev.f_relic.expose.failure: He answered smoothly and with injured dignity. You never did figure out who was right.
ev.f_relic.refuse: Don't buy: holy things are not for sale
ev.f_priest_omen.title: Bad signs
ev.f_priest_omen.text: A man of rank has made a lavish offering before an important venture and expects a favourable answer. But the signs could not be worse. He is looking at you, and a great deal depends on your words — including your place at the temple.
ev.f_priest_omen.truth.success: He put the venture off — and later thanked you: it would have ended in disaster. Your word is valued now.
ev.f_priest_omen.truth.failure: He stormed off to another priest, and your allowance was cut.
ev.f_priest_omen.soften: Find something favourable in the signs
ev.f_priest_poor_rite.title: A rite without payment
ev.f_priest_poor_rite.text: A poor widow begs you to perform the rite for her dead, but she has nothing to pay. At the same hour you are summoned to a wealthy house that promises a generous fee.
ev.f_priest_poor_rite.both: Manage both, however tired your legs
ev.f_ancestors.title: Duty to the ancestors
ev.f_ancestors.text: The day for honouring the ancestors has come, and the place where they are revered has fallen into disrepair. A worthy rite will not come cheap, but the ancestors see everything.
ev.f_ancestors.text.chinese_folk: The day of remembrance has come, and the ancestral hall is falling apart: the roof leaks and the memorial tablets have darkened. A proper rite and repairs will not come cheap.
ev.f_ancestors.text.andean: It is time to visit the ancestors' mummies: to dress them in new cloth, offer them chicha and carry them out for the festival. Good cloth is expensive.
ev.f_ancestors.text.african_traditional: The diviner says the ancestors are displeased: no one has brought them gifts for a long time. A memorial feast and an offering are needed, and that isn't cheap.
ev.f_ancestors.lavish: Do everything properly, whatever the cost
ev.f_ancestors.modest: A modest rite from a sincere heart
ev.f_ancestors.skip: Not this year: the living need the money more
ev.f_confession.title: Confession
ev.f_confession.text: At confession you admitted an old sin — a quarrel in which you were in the wrong, and the lie that grew out of it. The priest imposed a penance: forty days of fasting and prayer — and making peace.
ev.f_confession.donation: Ask to commute the penance into a gift to the church
ev.f_divination.title: Divination
ev.f_divination.text: An important venture lies ahead, and everyone advises you to learn the will of heaven first. The famous diviner charges a lot, but they say he is never wrong.
ev.f_divination.text.roman_gods: An important venture lies ahead, and everyone advises you to ask the gods first. For a fee, a haruspex will read the liver of a sacrificial animal, and an augur the flight of birds.
ev.f_divination.text.mesopotamian_gods: An important venture lies ahead, and everyone advises you to ask the gods first. A diviner-priest will examine a sacrificial lamb's liver and compare the signs with the clay tablets of omens.
ev.f_divination.text.chinese_folk: An important venture lies ahead, and everyone advises you to learn the will of Heaven first. A diviner will cast yarrow stalks according to the Book of Changes and check the days against the almanac.
ev.f_divination.text.shinto: An important venture lies ahead, and everyone advises you to learn the will of the kami first. An onmyoji diviner will calculate the auspicious day and direction.
ev.f_divination.diviner.success: The signs are favourable! You set about the venture with a light heart.
ev.f_divination.diviner.failure: The signs are bad. You put the venture off and still wonder whether you did the right thing.
ev.f_astrology.title: The astrologer
ev.f_astrology.text: A learned astrologer offers to cast your horoscope: under which stars you were born, when to begin ventures, what to beware of. Many respected people do nothing without his advice.
ev.f_astrology.text.dharmic: An astrologer offers to cast your horoscope from the positions of the planets at the hour of your birth: when to begin ventures, when to hold a wedding, what to beware of. Nothing important is done here without his advice.
ev.f_astrology.buy.ok: The horoscope promises a long life and success in business. Nice to hear, whatever you think of it.
ev.f_astrology.laugh: The stars are far away; the work is right here
ev.f_astrology.pious: The future is in the hands of higher powers, not astrologers
ev.f_holy_man.title: The wanderer
ev.f_holy_man.text: A strange man stands at the gate: barefoot, in rags, speaking in riddles, and looking at you as if he knows everything about you. The neighbours whisper that he is a saint — or just a madman. He asks for a night's lodging.
ev.f_holy_man.text.orthodox: A holy fool stands at the gate: barefoot in the cold, in chains, speaking in riddles and looking straight through you. The neighbours cross themselves. He asks for a night's lodging.
ev.f_holy_man.text.islamic: A dervish in a patched cloak with a begging bowl stands at the gate. He speaks in verse, laughs for no reason, and looks at you as if he knows everything about you. He asks for a night's lodging.
ev.f_holy_man.text.hindu: A sadhu stands at the gate — an ascetic smeared with ash, with a staff and a bowl. He says little but looks at you as if he knows everything about you. He asks for shelter for the night.
ev.f_holy_man.text.east_asian: A wandering monk in a tattered robe and straw hat stands at the gate. He speaks in riddles, laughs for no reason, and looks at you as if he knows everything about you. He asks for a night's lodging.
ev.f_holy_man.shelter: Let him in and feed him
ev.f_holy_man.alms: Give alms, but don't let him in
ev.f_holy_man.away: Send him away: all sorts wander about
ev.f_temple_build.title: A new temple
ev.f_temple_build.text: The community is raising funds for a new temple: the old one is falling apart and can't hold everyone. The names of generous donors, they say, will be carved in stone by the entrance.
ev.f_temple_build.text.islamic: The quarter is raising funds for a new mosque: the old one is falling apart and can't hold everyone on Fridays. The names of generous donors, they say, will be carved by the entrance.
ev.f_temple_build.text.jewish: The community is raising funds for a new synagogue: the old one is falling apart and can't hold everyone. The names of generous donors, they say, will be written in a book of remembrance.
ev.f_temple_build.text.christian: The parish is raising funds for a new church: the old one is falling apart and can't hold everyone. The names of generous donors, they say, will be remembered at every service.
ev.f_temple_build.big: Give a lot — let it stand for centuries
ev.f_temple_build.labour: Little money, but strong hands: work on the building
ev.f_holy_day_work.title: Work on a holy day
ev.f_holy_day_work.text: A lucrative job — but it means working on a holy day, when labour is a sin. The customer is in a hurry and pays double.
ev.f_holy_day_work.text.jewish: A lucrative job — but it means working on the Sabbath. The customer, of another faith, doesn't see the problem, is in a hurry and pays double.
ev.f_holy_day_work.text.christian: A lucrative job — but it means working on a Sunday, and a great feast day at that. The customer is in a hurry and pays double.
ev.f_holy_day_work.text.islamic: A lucrative job — but it means working through the Friday prayer. The customer is in a hurry and pays double.
ev.f_holy_day_work.refuse: Refuse: a holy day is a holy day
ev.f_holy_day_work.early: Get it all done the day before, without sleeping
ev.f_heresy.title: A new teaching
ev.f_heresy.text: People have appeared in town who interpret {faith} in their own way: simpler, stricter, without lavish rites and, as they put it, without corrupt clergy. You've been invited to one of their meetings.
ev.f_heresy.text.catholic: Wandering preachers teach that the true Church should be poor like the apostles, and that one can pray without lavish rites. You've been invited to their secret meeting.
ev.f_heresy.text.islamic: A Sufi brotherhood invites you to a night of dhikr: repeating the names of God for hours until your heart beats in time with them. Strict scholars eye them with suspicion.
ev.f_heresy.text.buddhist: A wandering monk teaches that sutras and rites are unnecessary: it is enough to repeat the name of Amida Buddha in faith, and salvation will come to anyone, even a sinner. The great monasteries are displeased.
ev.f_heresy.text.hindu: A wandering poet-saint sings that God loves everyone equally, the Brahmin and the poorest of the poor, and that temples and priests are not needed — only love. You've been invited to listen.
ev.f_heresy.listen: Listen once and keep your distance
ev.f_sacrifice.title: An offering to the gods
ev.f_sacrifice.text: Before sowing an offering is needed so the gods will grant a harvest. The best animal you own will please them most — and cost you most.
ev.f_sacrifice.text.hindu: Before an important undertaking a puja is needed: a priest, flowers, coconuts, oil for the lamps, a generous gift to the temple. You could do it more modestly — but the gods, they say, see the heart.
ev.f_sacrifice.text.mesoamerican: Before sowing the gods must be fed: copal, feathers, or better still your own blood, drawn from a pierced earlobe. The priest is waiting.
ev.f_sacrifice.text.andean: Before sowing a llama must be offered — the finest, without a single dark spot. Guinea pigs and chicha might do, but will that be pleasing?
ev.f_sacrifice.text.african_traditional: The diviner says the spirits need an offering before sowing: a goat, not a chicken — or the rains will pass your field by.
ev.f_sacrifice.best: Don't skimp: the best goes to the gods
ev.f_healing_shrine.title: Healing
ev.f_healing_shrine.text: The illness won't let go. They say that at a shrine outside town those the physicians have given up on are healed. The journey and the gifts are costly, and you have little strength.
ev.f_healing_shrine.text.roman_gods: The illness won't let go. They say that in the temple of Asclepius the sick sleep in the sacred portico, and the god comes to them in dreams to heal them. The journey and the gifts are costly.
ev.f_healing_shrine.text.christian: The illness won't let go. They say that at the relics of a saint in a distant monastery those the physicians have given up on are healed. The journey and the gifts are costly.
ev.f_healing_shrine.text.islamic: The illness won't let go. They say that at the tomb of a holy man outside town those the physicians have given up on are healed. The journey and the gifts are costly.
ev.f_healing_shrine.text.buddhist: The illness won't let go. They say that at the temple of the Medicine Buddha the monks chant sutras over the sick, and many get back on their feet. The journey and the gifts are costly.
ev.f_healing_shrine.go.success: After a few days at the shrine the fever broke, and for the first time in ages you woke up hungry and alert.
ev.f_healing_shrine.go.failure: The journey wore you out and no miracle came. But praying at the shrine gave you strength to endure.
ev.f_religious_school.title: The temple teacher
ev.f_religious_school.text: The teacher at the temple offers to teach you to read and to study the holy books. That means hours over letters instead of games and chores.
ev.f_religious_school.text.islamic: The teacher at the mosque offers to take you into the maktab: reading, writing and learning the Quran by heart. That means hours over a slate instead of games and chores.
ev.f_religious_school.text.jewish: The community's teacher offers to teach you to read the Torah. That means hours over letters instead of games and chores.
ev.f_religious_school.text.christian: The monks at the monastery teach children to read from the Psalter. They are willing to take you — hours over letters instead of games and chores.
ev.f_religious_school.text.chinese_folk: The village teacher offers to teach you characters and the classics of the sages. That means hours over a brush instead of games and chores.
ev.f_religious_school.no: There's enough work as it is
ev.f_debate.title: A debate of faiths
ev.f_debate.text: The ruler likes to hear learned men of different faiths debate. This time the lot of speaking for {faith} has fallen to you.
ev.f_debate.speak: Speak boldly and with all your strength
ev.f_debate.speak.success: You spoke so that the hall fell silent. The ruler nodded, and your words were argued over for a long time afterwards.
ev.f_debate.speak.failure: Your opponent was more skilful. You lost your thread, and even your own people chuckled at you.
ev.f_last_rites.title: Making ready
ev.f_last_rites.text: More and more you think about what waits beyond the threshold. You would like to meet it owing nothing — to people or to heaven.
ev.f_last_rites.donate: Leave the temple a gift for prayers of remembrance
ev.f_last_rites.forgive: Go round everyone you've quarrelled with and make peace
ev.f_last_rites.teach: Tell the young everything you know about faith and life
ev.f_last_rites.nothing: Live as you always have: what will be, will be
ev.f_min_tax.title: A special tax
ev.f_min_tax.text: The collector has come for the special tax that only those of other faiths pay. It is the price of the right to live here and pray in your own way, and this year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax.text.ISL: The collector has come for the jizya, the poll tax on non-Muslims. Pay it and you live under the protection of the law and pray in your own way. This year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax.plead: Plead for leniency: it's been a hard year
ev.f_min_tax.plead.success: The collector relented and reduced your share.
ev.f_min_tax.plead.failure: The collector took more than was due — for your impudence.
ev.f_min_tax.convert: Take up their faith — and pay no more
ev.f_min_tax_m.title: A special tax
ev.f_min_tax_m.text: The collector has come for the special tax that only those of other faiths pay. It is the price of the right to live here and pray in your own way, and this year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax_m.text.ISL: The collector has come for the jizya, the poll tax on non-Muslims. Pay it and you live under the protection of the law and pray in your own way. This year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax_m.plead: Plead for leniency: it's been a hard year
ev.f_min_tax_m.plead.success: The collector relented and reduced your share.
ev.f_min_tax_m.plead.failure: The collector took more than was due — for your impudence.
ev.f_min_tax_m.convert: Take up their faith — and pay no more
ev.f_min_tax_r.title: A special tax
ev.f_min_tax_r.text: The collector has come for the special tax that only those of other faiths pay. It is the price of the right to live here and pray in your own way, and this year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax_r.text.ISL: The collector has come for the jizya, the poll tax on non-Muslims. Pay it and you live under the protection of the law and pray in your own way. This year it has gone up again.
ev.f_min_tax_r.plead: Plead for leniency: it's been a hard year
ev.f_min_tax_r.plead.success: The collector relented and reduced your share.
ev.f_min_tax_r.plead.failure: The collector took more than was due — for your impudence.
ev.f_min_tax_r.convert: Take up their faith — and pay no more
ev.f_min_riot.title: The riot
ev.f_min_riot.text: A rumour crept through the town that the troubles of recent months are the fault of the unbelievers. In the evening a crowd with clubs set off for the quarter where people of your faith live.
ev.f_min_riot.hide.success: You spent the night in an acquaintance's cellar. In the morning your home had been looted, but you were alive.
ev.f_min_riot.hide.failure: They found you. You got away with a beating, but the house burned down.
ev.f_min_riot.defend: Stand with the neighbours and block the street
ev.f_min_riot.defend.success: You stood shoulder to shoulder, and the crowd milled about and fell back. The quarter will not forget it.
ev.f_min_riot.defend.failure: The crowd broke through. You barely survived.
ev.f_min_riot.authorities: Run to the authorities and beg for protection
ev.f_min_riot.authorities.success: The guards scattered the crowd — this time.
ev.f_min_riot.authorities.failure: The guards arrived when it was all over.
ev.f_min_riot_m.title: The riot
ev.f_min_riot_m.text: A rumour crept through the town that the troubles of recent months are the fault of the unbelievers. In the evening a crowd with clubs set off for the quarter where people of your faith live.
ev.f_min_riot_m.hide.success: You spent the night in an acquaintance's cellar. In the morning your home had been looted, but you were alive.
ev.f_min_riot_m.hide.failure: They found you. You got away with a beating, but the house burned down.
ev.f_min_riot_m.defend: Stand with the neighbours and block the street
ev.f_min_riot_m.defend.success: You stood shoulder to shoulder, and the crowd milled about and fell back. The quarter will not forget it.
ev.f_min_riot_m.defend.failure: The crowd broke through. You barely survived.
ev.f_min_riot_m.authorities: Run to the authorities and beg for protection
ev.f_min_riot_m.authorities.success: The guards scattered the crowd — this time.
ev.f_min_riot_m.authorities.failure: The guards arrived when it was all over.

ev.f_min_forced.title: Convert or leave
ev.f_min_forced.text: A decree has gone out: whoever does not accept the faith of the majority must leave the land by the end of the year. At night the neighbours whisper about who will choose what.
ev.f_min_forced.secret: Accept it outwardly, but keep praying as before — in secret
ev.f_min_forced.refuse.success: In your district the decree was never enforced — for now. You held firm.
ev.f_min_forced.refuse.failure: Your property was seized and you were thrown into prison for half a year. You did not give in.

ev.f_min_hide.title: Hiding your faith
ev.f_min_hide.text: You've been offered a good position, in a guild or in service. There's one condition: they only take people of the majority faith. No one will ask directly — it's enough to keep quiet and behave 'like everyone else'.
ev.f_min_hide.pretend: Keep quiet and behave like everyone else

ev.f_min_flee.title: Leave?
ev.f_min_flee.text: Year by year life grows narrower: new prohibitions, sidelong looks, rumours of riots in nearby towns. Many who share your faith have already left for places where they are left alone. They are calling you too.
ev.f_min_flee.wait: Wait: perhaps it will blow over

ev.f_min_patron.title: A patron
ev.f_min_patron.text: An influential man of another faith offers you his protection: under his wing no one will touch you. In return he expects loyal service, gifts on feast days — and perhaps something more in the future.
ev.f_min_patron.refuse: Refuse: I don't want to be in anyone's debt
ev.f_min_patron.community: Rely on your own — the community will protect you

ev.f_min_books.title: The books
ev.f_min_books.text: The authorities have ordered the holy books of your faith collected and burned: they say the books slander the majority's faith. Today the guards are going from house to house in your quarter.
ev.f_min_books.hide: Hide the books under the floor
ev.f_min_books.hide.success: The books lay in their hiding place until better days.
ev.f_min_books.hide.failure: The hiding place was found. The books were burned, and you were fined and threatened with worse.
ev.f_min_books.give: Hand them over: life is worth more
ev.f_min_books.memorize: Learn as much as you can by heart, then hand them over

ev.f_min_convert_offer.title: Open doors
ev.f_min_convert_offer.text: An acquaintance from the majority says in a friendly way: 'Join our faith and every door will open. Office, trade, a good match. Why be an outsider all your life?'
ev.f_min_convert_offer.refuse: Refuse: I am who I am
ev.f_min_convert_offer.think: Laugh it off and change the subject

ev.f_min_mocked.title: Mockery
ev.f_min_mocked.text: In the street people laugh at you: at your clothes, your prayers, what you eat and don't eat. Today some boys shouted insults after you, and the grown-ups pretended not to hear.
ev.f_min_mocked.answer.success: The boys went quiet and didn't bother you again.
ev.f_min_mocked.answer.failure: It came to blows, and somehow you were the one who got blamed.
ev.f_min_mocked.explain: Calmly explain what your customs mean
ev.f_min_mocked.endure: Bear it and walk past in silence
ev.f_min_friend.title: Neighbours
ev.f_min_friend.text: A neighbour of another faith brought a dish of his own cooking for your feast day, with a bow and an awkward smile. His people look askance at him, and yours at you.
ev.f_min_friend.refuse: Politely decline: it's safer that way
ev.f_m_min_quarter.text.1: In your quarter everyone knows everyone: who has had a baby, who is ill, who is getting married. The foreign city begins just around the corner.
ev.f_m_min_quarter.text.2: On your feast day you prayed in low voices behind closed shutters. But afterwards you sang — quietly, but all together.
ev.f_m_min_their_feast.text: The majority are celebrating a great feast of {other_faith} today: the streets are full of lights and music, everyone in their best clothes. You watched from the doorway — beautiful, joyful, and not yours at all.
ev.f_m_min_two_names.text: You have two names: one for your own people, another for outsiders — for the market and the court. You've long since learned to answer to both.
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.title: A pilgrim's tale
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.text: Years have passed, and the young still ask you to tell them about your pilgrimage. In memory the road has grown longer, the bandits fiercer, the wonders brighter.
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.true: Tell it as it was — blisters, fear and all
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.embellish: Embellish it: let them listen open-mouthed
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.embellish.success: Your listeners are enthralled, and now you're invited to every gathering.
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.embellish.failure: One of the listeners had been there himself and caught you out in front of everyone.
ev.f_pilgrim_memory.inspire: Persuade the young to make the journey themselves
ev.f_convert_friends.title: Former brethren
ev.f_convert_friends.text: Ever since you changed your faith, old friends turn away in the street, and someone has spread a rumour that you sold yourself. Only one old acquaintance came to talk.
ev.f_convert_friends.explain.success: He listened and understood. At least one bridge still stands.
ev.f_convert_friends.explain.failure: The talk ended in shouting. He won't come again.
ev.f_convert_friends.cut: Don't justify yourself: this is my path
ev.f_convert_friends.gift: Help their community with money, without fuss
ev.f_convert_kin.title: Blood ties
ev.f_convert_kin.text: {npc}, your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister}, hasn't spoken to you since you changed your faith. Today you came face to face in the street.
ev.f_convert_kin.reach.success: An awkward silence, then tears — and an embrace. Your faiths are different now, but your blood is the same.
ev.f_convert_kin.reach.failure: {npc} turned away and left without a word.
ev.f_convert_kin.gift: Send a gift for {g=npc_sex:his|her} feast day
ev.f_secret_faith_later.title: The secret
ev.f_secret_faith_later.text: A neighbour has noticed that you still keep the old rites — quietly, behind closed shutters. She is looking at you expectantly.
ev.f_secret_faith_later.deny.success: She shrugged and never brought it up again.
ev.f_secret_faith_later.deny.failure: Her report reached the authorities. A fine, and disgrace before the whole quarter.
ev.f_secret_faith_later.give_up: Give up the old rites: enough living in fear
ev.f_hidden_exposed.title: Exposed
ev.f_hidden_exposed.text: Someone has reported that you don't actually hold the faith you claim. At work there are sidelong glances, and your superiors demand an explanation.
ev.f_hidden_exposed.confess: Confess and leave with your honour
ev.f_hidden_exposed.talk: Talk your way out: it's slander
ev.f_hidden_exposed.talk.failure: They didn't believe you. You were thrown out in disgrace and not paid for the last months.
ev.f_heresy_trial.title: The accusation
ev.f_heresy_trial.text: You've been summoned before the clergy: they say you attended the gatherings of false teachers. They demand names and repentance.
ev.f_heresy_trial.text.islamic: The qadi has summoned you: they say words unfit for a believer were spoken at your night gatherings. They demand names and repentance.
ev.f_heresy_trial.text.buddhist: The authorities have banned the gatherings of the new teaching's followers. You've been summoned and told to renounce it and give names.
ev.f_heresy_trial.recant.success: You were released with an order to keep away from such gatherings in future.
ev.f_heresy_trial.recant.failure: They didn't believe you and imposed a heavy fine.
ev.f_heresy_trial.stand.success: Your steadfastness unsettled the judges, and you were released. People whisper about it with respect.
ev.f_heresy_trial.stand.failure: You were imprisoned for a year and stripped of almost everything you owned. But you did not recant.
ev.f_vow_reminder.title: The unkept vow
ev.f_vow_reminder.text: Misfortunes come one after another, and at night you remember the vow you made in that storm and never kept.
ev.f_holy_man_return.title: The wanderer's blessing
ev.f_holy_man_return.text: The wanderer you once sheltered is at your gate again — and now he is revered as a saint throughout the district. He recognised you and blessed your house in front of everyone.
ev.f_holy_man_return.feast: Thank him and hold a meal in his honour
ev.f_monk_abbot.title: The community decides
ev.f_monk_abbot.text: The old {g:abbot|abbess} has died, and the community wants you to take {g:his|her} place. That means authority, estates, lands, quarrels with the powerful — and far less silence.
ev.f_monk_abbot.decline: Decline: I didn't come here for power
ev.f_temple_name.title: A name in stone
ev.f_temple_name.text: The new temple has been consecrated. The donors' names have been recorded for posterity, and yours is among the first. People stop to read them and nod to you in the street.
ev.f_temple_name.humble: Ask not to be named: the gift wasn't for glory
